dimensions.note: The report holds no credentials and makes no authenticated call — it reads resource snapshots the model already wrote. One dependency is worth stating rather than assuming: findings can carry a rung's `detail`, which is a slice of restic's stderr, and restic echoes its configuration into error messages. That stderr is redacted at the model's subprocess boundary before it is ever persisted, and that redaction is mutation-proven in the model's own harness. The report cannot re-redact — it never sees the secrets — so it inherits the guarantee rather than enforcing it. If the model's redaction ever regressed, this report would propagate the leak into a findings list.

Emits no log lines, matching @sntxrr/b2/fleet-hygiene, which also emits none. For a report the markdown and JSON output IS the user-visible record, and the entry/completion logging convention exists for methods that otherwise leave no trace. Nothing is logged, so nothing sensitive can be logged.

Deliberately never throws, and this is a reasoned divergence from the narrow-try/catch guidance. A workflow-scope report that throws takes the workflow's summary down with it, which would destroy the audit trail for exactly the run that had a problem. `readSnapshot` and `readStandingRecord` catch broadly and return null — but the failure is NOT swallowed: a null repository snapshot degrades that repository to `scanned: false`, which raises a `repo-unreachable` finding and flips `fleetScanComplete` to false. The error becomes a visible finding rather than a silent omission. Proven by execution: MECH#5 drives a context whose getContent rejects every call and asserts the run still completes with repositoriesScanned 0 and fleetScanComplete false.

25 unit tests plus 12 mechanical checks, both verified by exit status. `analyze` is pure and exported so findings are tested against hand-built state without a workflow context, and `execute` is tested against a stub context covering the succeeded, failed-step, standing-record and datastore-down paths. Three honesty guards are mutation-proven — silencing the dormant-exclusion finding, dropping the modelType fallback for failed steps, and hardcoding standingRecordsReadable to true each fail the suite.

Pure with respect to the world: it writes nothing, mutates nothing and calls no external service, so re-running it over the same execution yields the same output. Partial failure is the normal case rather than an edge case — a fleet run where some repositories failed is expected, and the report is built to describe that state accurately rather than to require completeness.

No HTTP calls, but there is one real unverified contract and the report's headline finding depends on it. `readStandingRecord` calls `dataRepository.getContent(modelType, modelId, instanceName)` with NO version, expecting the latest snapshot of an instance THIS run may not have written — that is what lets a restore proven last week avoid being reported as never proven. The swamp docs describe getContent as covering a report's own execution; whether a workflow-scope report may resolve a prior instance is NOT live-verified, and mock tests cannot settle it because the mock is what I wrote. The design fails safe: if every standing read returns null or throws, `standingRecordsReadable` goes false, the report says so at the top, and every finding rewords from 'never proven' to 'not proven in this run' — so the worst case is a louder report, never a falsely reassuring one. Recorded as an ISSUE rather than a pass because until the first live fleet run confirms it, the nightly output may be more alarming than the truth. This is the b2-transfer lesson applied in advance: the mocks were built from the docs, so they tested the docs.
Holds no network connections, file handles or temporary files. Reads are awaited sequentially per step; nothing is left open on any path, including the error paths, because there is nothing to close.

Audited with the same method as the model extension: 49 real identifiers from the live inventory (25 B2 bucket names, 24 ansible hostnames) plus known short host names grepped against every file in the extension and its mechanical harness. The only match is `/var/lib/docker`, a filesystem path rather than the host or bucket of the same name. Fixtures and the README's sample output use fictional bird-named repositories (heron-debian, mallard-ubuntu, teal-debian) and host.example.net, consistent with the sanitisation already applied across this repo's history.
